summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on embedded firmware experience across STM32, Jetson, and Arduino platforms. Built concurrent, multithreaded firmware using FreeRTOS with mutex-based task coordination and interrupt-driven UART/I2C/SPI communication for real-time sensor processing. Led first-of-kind board bring-up for a human-subjects research rig in C++, adding ACK-based command reliability, timeout/retry logic, and brown-out reset detection over USB.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux; drove real-time sensor processing for a Jetson+Arduino controller.
Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a systemd service with static IP networking and XRDP remote administration of the headless Jetson.
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection.

projects.name: Haptics Research Study Controller — Embedded Rig + PyQt6 Host
bullets: Rebuilt a human-subjects haptics rig (Peltier element, 3 vibrotactile actuators, NTC thermistor) as an Arduino executor with a direction-aware temperature killswitch and a cross-platform PyQt6 host, eliminating a silent failure in which the prior Web Serial app left actuators running.
Moved the host safety cutoff into a dedicated serial QThread; added command-level reliability with echo matching, a 400 ms ACK timeout, 3 retries, and brown-out reset detection.
Built a 36-trial state machine with hold/resume across USB dropouts and crash-safe queued logging of a 10 Hz temperature trace; shipped Windows and macOS builds with PyInstaller.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
